title: Iran developing first domestically built nuclear fusion reactor: state media
site_name: Gulf News: Latest UAE news, Dubai news, Business, travel news, Dubai Gold rate, prayer time, cinema
excerpt: Iran unveils plans for its first domestically built nuclear fusion reactor, showcasing indigenous technology and scientific progress, according to state media.
content:
Iran is developing its first domestically built nuclear fusion reactor using entirely indigenous technology, the head of the country's Atomic Energy Organisation (AEOI), Mohammad Eslami, said on Sunday.

“We hope to bring the first Iranian tokamak, built entirely with domestic expertise, into operation according to the planned schedule,” Eslami said in a televised interview.

He said Iranian scientists had made significant progress in developing the system, describing the project as evidence of the country's ability to compete with technologically advanced nations, according to state media.

The planned reactor will use tokamak technology, a magnetic-confinement system designed to contain extremely hot plasma and facilitate nuclear fusion — the process that powers the Sun and other stars.

Unlike conventional nuclear fission reactors, which generate energy by splitting heavy atomic nuclei, fusion reactors seek to release energy by combining lighter nuclei.

The technology has the potential to provide large amounts of low-carbon energy, although commercial-scale fusion power remains technically challenging and has yet to become a widely established source of electricity.

Eslami did not disclose the reactor's planned capacity, location, construction cost or expected commissioning date.

Nuclear fusion is distinct from Iran's existing uranium-enrichment programme.

Developing a tokamak does not, by itself, demonstrate progress towards producing a nuclear weapon. It is a separate scientific and energy research field.
